commit 317b51f2ad0894b4e7eea33e41938806551c3892
Author: Andy Wilkinson <awilkinson@pivotal.io>
Date:   Wed Mar 7 09:57:16 2018 +0000

    Make ApplicationContextRequestMatcher and subclasses thread-safe
    
    Previously, when performing lazy initialisation of the context,
    ApplicationContextRequestMatcher assigned the context field before it
    called initialized. The context being non-null is used as the signal
    that it’s ok to call a subclass’s matches method. If one thread checks
    for a non-null context in between the field being assigned and
    initialized being called on another thread, matches will be called
    before the subclass is ready.
    
    This commit closes the window for the race condition by only assigning
    the context field once the subclass’s initialized method has been
    called.
    
    There is a secondary problem in each of the subclasses. Due to the use
    of double-checked locking in ApplicationContextRequestMatcher, it’s
    possible for a subclass’s matches method to be called by a thread that
    has not synchronised on the context lock that’s held when initialized
    is called and the delegate field is assigned. This means that the
    value assigned to the field may not be visible to that thread.
    
    This commit declares the delegate field of each
    ApplicationContextRequestMatcher subclass as volatile to ensure that,
    following initialisation, its value is guaranteed to be visible to
    all threads.
    
    Closes gh-12380

diff --git a/spring-boot-project/spring-boot/src/main/java/org/springframework/boot/security/servlet/ApplicationContextRequestMatcher.java b/spring-boot-project/spring-boot/src/main/java/org/springframework/boot/security/servlet/ApplicationContextRequestMatcher.java
index 84441b3eb4..11d29b1d25 100644
--- a/spring-boot-project/spring-boot/src/main/java/org/springframework/boot/security/servlet/ApplicationContextRequestMatcher.java
+++ b/spring-boot-project/spring-boot/src/main/java/org/springframework/boot/security/servlet/ApplicationContextRequestMatcher.java
@@ -69,8 +69,9 @@ public abstract class ApplicationContextRequestMatcher<C> implements RequestMatc
 		if (this.context == null) {
 			synchronized (this.contextLock) {
 				if (this.context == null) {
-					this.context = createContext(request);
-					initialized(this.context);
+					Supplier<C> createdContext = createContext(request);
+					initialized(createdContext);
+					this.context = createdContext;
 				}
 			}
 		}

`AtomicBoolean.compareAndSet(false, true)`, which introduced the race: `compareAndSet` returns immediately, so a second concurrent thread s

ees `initialized == true` and proceeds to call `matches()` while the first thread is still inside `initialized(context)`.

to a `synchronized`/double-checked-locking pattern. I inspected each prior commit touching this file to find where the `AtomicBoolean` pattern was introduced.

Contrast with the prior version (introduced in `317b51f

Found it. Commit `5938ca78b6` rewrote the matcher's locking mechanism from a synchronized double-checked-locking pattern to `AtomicBoolean.compareAndSet(false, true)`, which introduced the race: `compareAndSet` returns immediately, so a second concurrent thread sees `initialized == true` and proceeds to call `matches()` while the first thread is still inside `initialized(context)`.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 5938ca78b6e6bd86364b6fdae7a84fcf7f65e761

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** I traced the file history of `ApplicationContextRequestMatcher.java` with `git log --follow`. The fix commit (`f03ca7e175`) reverts an `AtomicBoolean`-based `compareAndSet` pattern back to a `synchronized`/double-checked-locking pattern. I inspected each prior commit touching this file to find where the `AtomicBoolean` pattern was introduced.

**(2) The introducing change:** Commit `5938ca78b6` ("Fix request matcher management context support") rewrote `matches(HttpServletRequest)`:

```java
if (this.initialized.compareAndSet(false, true)) {
    initialized(context);
}
return matches(request, context);
```

`compareAndSet(false, true)` atomically flips the flag to `true` *before* `initialized(context)` runs. Any other thread calling `matches()` concurrently will see `initialized == true` immediately, skip the `initialized(context)` call, and proceed straight to `matches(request, context)` — even though the first thread's `initialized(context)` call hasn't returned yet. This is exactly the race gh-18211 describes.

Contrast with the prior version (introduced in `317b51f2ad`), which used a `synchronized` block with double-checked locking on a `context`/`contextLock` field — a second thread would block on the monitor until `initialized()` completed and the field was assigned, so it couldn't proceed early.

The fix commit's own new test (`matchesWhenConcurrentlyCalledWaitsForInitialize`) directly targets this scenario: two threads call `matches()` concurrently, `initialized()` sleeps 200ms, and `matches()` asserts `initialized` is true — this test would fail against the `AtomicBoolean.compareAndSet` implementation from `5938ca78b6` but passes with the `synchronized`-based fix.

**(3) Evidence:** 
- The diff of the fix commit removes `AtomicBoolean` and the `compareAndSet` check, replacing it with `volatile boolean initialized` + `synchronized (initializeLock)` double-checked locking — a direct structural reversion of the pattern introduced in `5938ca78b6`.
- The commit message of `5938ca78b6` doesn't mention thread-safety concerns at all — it was focused on management-context caching (gh-18012) — indicating the race condition was an unintended side effect of that refactor rather than a deliberate (and reviewed) concurrency design.

I'm highly confident in this identification since the mechanism (compareAndSet vs. synchronized block) is a clear, isolated, and well-understood concurrency bug pattern, and the fix's added test exercises exactly this window.
